spreadsheet-guide.title: How to Use a Superbuy Spreadsheet: A Practical Guide
spreadsheet-guide.description: Find current listings, record the right variant, review warehouse photos and plan an Indonesia parcel with a clear next action.

sections.heading: A spreadsheet is a starting point, not a quality guarantee
paragraphs: A useful Superbuy spreadsheet solves one problem: discovery. It turns a long list of Chinese marketplace listings into a cleaner set of product and category routes. That can save time, especially when a product title is difficult to search in English. It does not prove that a listing is current, that every variant is available, or that the seller will send exactly what appears in an old photo. Treating a spreadsheet as a recommendation certificate is the fastest way to skip the checks that matter.

The safer approach is to separate discovery from verification. Use the spreadsheet to find a candidate. Then open the current destination listing and make a fresh decision from the live information. Check the selected colour, size, model, quantity, seller notes and domestic shipping cost. If the page has changed since the index was updated, the live listing wins. This simple rule prevents most spreadsheet-related confusion before money is committed.

sections.heading: Search narrowly and compare more than one route
paragraphs: Begin with a specific need rather than browsing everything. A query such as “black zip hoodie” or “white low-profile trainers” produces a more manageable shortlist than a broad word such as “clothes.” Category pages are useful when you want ideas, but keyword search is better when fit, material or colour is important. Open two or three plausible listings and compare them side by side instead of choosing the first attractive image.

Compare what can actually be verified: the product description, option names, measurements, sales information shown by the source marketplace, seller terms and recent listing images. A lower item price may come with paid domestic delivery, fewer useful measurements or weak return conditions. A slightly higher price can be easier to evaluate if the listing explains variants clearly. The goal is not to find the cheapest card in the index; it is to find a listing whose details you can understand and later verify.

sections.heading: Record the exact variant before you order
paragraphs: Before submitting an order, create a short decision record. Save the product URL and note the colour, size, quantity and any message that must be passed to the seller. For clothing, save the size chart and compare garment measurements with something you already own. Letter sizes are inconsistent across sellers, so “M” on one listing can be close to “S” or “L” elsewhere. For shoes, confirm whether the option uses EU sizing, foot length or an internal code.

This record becomes your QC reference. When warehouse photos arrive several days later, you should not have to rely on memory. You can compare the label, colour and visible construction with what you selected. It also helps if an agent asks for clarification because the option names are ambiguous. A precise order remark is useful; a long message full of assumptions is not. Ask for one measurable or visible requirement at a time.
bullets: Any seller promise that affects the order

sections.heading: Understand the two payment stages
paragraphs: Superbuy’s current fee guide separates the process into purchasing and international shipping. During the purchasing stage, the user pays the item price and any domestic delivery charge from the seller to the warehouse. The guide says standard purchasing from mainstream platforms such as Taobao, Tmall, JD and 1688 has no purchasing service fee, while second-hand or unlisted platforms can have different charges. Optional services, such as extra photographs or specialized inspection, are separate choices.

International delivery is a later payment. It is not included in the price shown on a spreadsheet card. The final parcel cost depends on destination, route, chargeable weight, dimensions and any selected parcel services. Keeping these stages separate makes budgeting more realistic. A low product price can still result in an expensive parcel if the item is bulky, heavy or restricted to a limited set of routes.

sections.heading: Use warehouse photos as a structured checkpoint
paragraphs: Superbuy’s current homepage states that free QC photos are taken after warehouse inspection. Those images are valuable because they show the received item before international shipping. Compare them with your decision record. Start with the label and selected variant, then check the overall shape, visible colour, quantity shown, printing, obvious damage and included accessories. Do not begin by zooming into a minor stitch while ignoring that the wrong size has arrived.

The photographs have limits. A standard visual inspection cannot confirm hidden materials, internal electronics, authenticity or long-term durability. Warehouse lighting and image compression can also alter colour. If a specific detail controls your decision and the standard photos do not show it, request a targeted detailed photo before approving the item. Paying for one useful angle is often better than ordering several vague images.

sections.heading: Use the storage window to consolidate deliberately
paragraphs: Superbuy’s current fee structure states that items receive 90 days of free storage after arrival. It also says storage beyond that period is charged daily and that the normal maximum storage period is 180 days unless an extension is arranged. That does not mean every buyer should wait for three months. It means there is room to receive several orders, resolve QC issues and combine suitable items into a parcel.

Consolidation can reduce duplicated base charges, but adding more items is not automatically cheaper. Large shoe boxes, rigid packaging and low-density goods may increase volumetric weight. Use the warehouse period to decide what belongs together, not as a reason to keep shopping indefinitely. Check the storage deadline shown in the account and submit the parcel with enough time to resolve any problem.

sections.heading: Plan the parcel before choosing the cheapest line
paragraphs: At parcel submission, compare the routes available for the actual contents and destination. Look beyond the headline price. Check whether the route accepts the item category, how it calculates chargeable weight, what tracking is provided, the expected range rather than a single promised day, and what compensation or insurance terms apply. Customs duties and VAT depend on the destination and declaration rules, and the recipient remains responsible for complying with local law.

Packaging decisions should match the risk. Removing unnecessary retail packaging may reduce weight or volume for flexible clothing. Fragile goods may need bubble cushioning, corner protection, foam filling or a stronger outer box. Superbuy lists these as optional value-added services, so choose them because the item needs them—not because a long list of services looks reassuring.

sections.heading: Common spreadsheet mistakes to avoid
paragraphs: The first common mistake is assuming that an old price is still available. The second is choosing a variant from the card image without reading the live option menu. The third is approving QC photos without comparing them to the original selection. The fourth is treating estimated international shipping as a fixed quote. The fifth is waiting until the storage deadline to ask about a problem. Each mistake comes from skipping a transition between discovery, ordering, warehousing and delivery.

A spreadsheet works best when those transitions are explicit. Find the listing, verify it, record the variant, check the warehouse photos, then build the parcel. If any stage creates uncertainty, stop there rather than carrying the uncertainty into an international shipment. This workflow is slower than one-click browsing, but it is much faster than correcting a wrong item after it has crossed a border.

sections.heading: A practical final checklist
paragraphs: Before ordering, confirm the live listing, option, measurement and seller terms. Before approving warehouse QC, match the visible item with the saved order record and request one targeted photo if a decisive detail is missing. Before shipping, check storage deadlines, parcel contents, route restrictions, packaging, estimated chargeable weight and destination tax responsibilities. Keep screenshots of the order and final parcel details until delivery is complete.

The best Superbuy spreadsheet is not the one with the most links. It is the one that helps you move from a broad search to a small number of verifiable choices. Use it as an organized map, keep your own notes, and let current listing data and visible warehouse evidence guide the decision.

sections.heading: Keep an Indonesia shortlist with a next action
paragraphs: For each candidate, record the current listing URL, option, measurement, price currency and date checked. Add one next action: clarify a variant, compare a measurement, check available shipping or discard the candidate. A short list with resolved questions is more useful than a large collection of unverified links. Keep catalog discovery separate from your service account: product links here open cnfanshp.com, while Superbuy payments and warehouse actions belong in the appropriate account.

Before moving a candidate into an order, reserve a separate amount for international delivery and Indonesia import costs. Use the payment guide when comparing debit and credited amounts, the shoe guide when a size chart is unclear, and the warehouse guide when several items are ready. Those decisions have different evidence requirements; one attractive product card cannot settle them all.

qc-photo-checklist.title: Superbuy QC Photos: What to Check Before Shipping
qc-photo-checklist.description: Check size labels, quantities and visible condition, request useful additional photos, and record a warehouse decision before shipping.
secondaryKeywords: how to read Superbuy QC photos

sections.heading: Why QC photos deserve a real process
paragraphs: Warehouse QC photos are the last practical chance to catch many visible problems before an item enters international delivery. They are not decorative order updates. They connect the listing you selected with the physical item that reached the warehouse. A good review can identify the wrong colour, wrong size label, missing accessory, obvious stain, damaged box or visibly different design while there may still be time to ask for help.

A poor review usually has one of two problems. The buyer looks only for a dramatic defect, or the buyer expects the photos to prove things a camera cannot prove. The better method is structured: compare order facts first, then overall shape, then specific details, and finally decide whether the remaining uncertainty is acceptable.

sections.heading: Know what the standard service actually includes
paragraphs: Superbuy’s current homepage says warehouse inspection includes free QC photos. Its forwarding guide also describes three photographs of the actual product after warehousing. The current fee page lists paid options for detailed photos, re-inspection, detailed inspection, power-on checks, video shooting and model try-on photographs. These are separate services for cases where the standard view is not enough.

The existence of extra services explains the boundary of a standard check. A routine visual inspection is designed to confirm obvious, visible information. It is not a laboratory test and it does not convert a third-party marketplace listing into a guaranteed product. Superbuy’s own purchasing notices say it provides an agent service and does not assume the seller’s product-quality risk. That distinction should shape every QC decision.

sections.heading: Prepare before the photos arrive
paragraphs: QC begins at ordering. Save the live listing, selected colour, size, quantity and any relevant seller chart. If a product is customized, save the exact agreed instruction. Without that reference, a warehouse image can show a perfectly clear label and still leave you unable to tell whether it is the label you ordered.

Choose two or three decisive checks in advance. For a hoodie, they might be size label, front print placement and colour. For shoes, they might be size tag, outsole shape and pair symmetry. For a collectible, they might be outer-box condition, included parts and seal status. This prevents random zooming and helps you request a precise additional photo when needed.

sections.heading: The first pass: identity, variant and quantity
paragraphs: Start with identity. Does the item in the warehouse image match the product type and model ordered? Then confirm the visible option. Read the size label, colour name, model code or other mark when available. If multiple pieces were ordered, check whether the photos or warehouse record show the expected quantity. Do not assume that a similar colour or a familiar logo means the correct variant arrived.

If a label is too small to read, that is a good reason for a targeted photo. Ask for the size tag or model code to fill the frame. Avoid vague requests such as “take better photos,” because the result may still miss the evidence you need. One clear request creates a checkable result.

sections.heading: The second pass: shape, symmetry and visible condition
paragraphs: Next, step back and compare the whole item. Look for left-right symmetry, a straight neckline, evenly placed pockets, matching shoe shapes, aligned panels and an undamaged silhouette. Creases caused by folding are not automatically defects, but deep dents, crushed structural parts or a visibly warped shape deserve attention. Compare every available angle before deciding.

Then scan the surface. Check for stains, scratches, missing paint, broken hardware, loose components, severe print misalignment and obvious tears. Warehouse lighting can create reflections, especially on leather-like materials, metal and glossy packaging. If a mark appears in one image but disappears from another angle, request a close-up rather than guessing.

sections.heading: Clothing checks that photographs can support
paragraphs: For clothing, verify the visible size tag and compare the general cut with the listing. Look at print or embroidery placement, collar shape, cuffs, hem, zipper direction, pocket position and colour blocking. A standard photo rarely gives reliable garment measurements unless a ruler is deliberately included, so do not estimate exact chest width from perspective alone.

Colour is also imperfect evidence. Different lamps, phone screens and compression can shift navy toward black or cream toward white. Use colour photos to identify a clear mismatch, not to judge a subtle shade with absolute certainty. If the shade is critical, ask for a photograph under neutral lighting or beside a simple colour reference, while accepting that screens still vary.

sections.heading: Shoe, accessory and electronics checks
paragraphs: For shoes, check that both shoes are present, the size labels agree, the pair appears symmetrical and the outsole, heel, toe box and fastening system match the ordered model. If keeping the retail box matters, inspect its condition separately from the shoes. A damaged box and an undamaged product are different decisions.

For bags and accessories, focus on visible hardware, strap count, closures, included pouches and surface condition. For electronics, standard appearance photos do not prove function. Superbuy’s current value-added list includes a paid power-on inspection for certain devices, which checks basic indicator and power functions. Even that is a limited functional check, not a complete durability or battery-health test.

sections.heading: What QC photos cannot confirm
paragraphs: A photograph cannot reliably confirm material composition, internal construction, waterproofing, battery capacity, electrical safety, scent, taste or long-term durability. It cannot prove authenticity simply because visible branding looks familiar. It also cannot guarantee that an item will survive international transport. Packaging and route risk are separate decisions made later.

Bulk and sealed goods have additional limits. Superbuy’s 1688 guidance says original packaging may not be opened to count individual units when quantity is not shown externally, and service levels vary by seller classification. Second-hand products can also have restricted or unavailable return options. Read the service warning attached to the order instead of assuming every marketplace receives the same inspection.

sections.heading: When an extra photo is worth paying for
paragraphs: Request an additional photo when one visible fact will decide whether you keep or return the item. Good examples include a readable size label, the back print, a serial or model code, a close-up of a suspected stain, the contents laid out together, or a ruler placed across a specific measurement. The current Superbuy fee page lists detailed photographs as a per-photo optional service, so a precise request also controls cost.

Do not buy extra photos merely to reduce a feeling of uncertainty that no image can resolve. If your concern is hidden material quality or authenticity, more angles of the exterior may not answer it. Decide whether the remaining risk is acceptable, whether the seller’s return terms allow action, or whether the item should not be ordered in the first place.

sections.heading: Approve, ask, or escalate: a simple decision rule
paragraphs: Approve when the visible identity, variant, quantity and condition match your record and the unverified qualities are risks you knowingly accept. Ask for a targeted photo when a specific visible fact is missing or unclear. Contact after-sales support when the existing images show a clear mismatch, damage or missing component. Provide the order number and state the observable issue without exaggeration.

Finally, save the key photos and your decision until the parcel is delivered. If a later problem occurs, a clear record of what entered the parcel is more useful than memory. QC is not about finding perfection in every stitch. It is about making the best evidence-based decision while the item is still at the warehouse.

sections.heading: Write an actionable QC decision
paragraphs: Record the order reference, the selected variant, the visible finding and the next action. For example, an unreadable size label is a request for a closer image; a clearly different label is a mismatch to raise with support. Keep those cases separate. Describe what the photograph shows instead of adding a claim about hidden material or authenticity. Save the image and the reply so the decision can be understood when packing begins.

For footwear, check both labels and distinguish foot length from insole or outsole measurements. For a mixed parcel, finish each unresolved QC decision before consolidation. A stored item can be physically ready to pack while still awaiting your approval. Use the specialist shoe and warehouse guides to complete those steps, then preserve the record until delivery and any related support case are resolved.

shipping-cost-guide.title: Superbuy Shipping Cost: Deposit, Weight and Final Charge
shipping-cost-guide.description: Compare actual and volumetric weight, shipping deposits and final charges, with an Indonesia parcel planning checklist.

sections.heading: Why the first number is not the whole cost
paragraphs: A product card price tells you almost nothing about the final delivered cost. Shopping through an agent has at least two financial stages: getting the item from a Chinese seller to the warehouse, and getting the finished parcel from the warehouse to an overseas address. Optional inspection, photography and packaging services can add a third layer. Confusing these stages is why a cheap item can produce an unexpectedly expensive total.

Superbuy’s current fee structure describes the same separation. Stage one includes product price, domestic delivery and any applicable purchasing or value-added service. Stage two is international shipping, calculated from the parcel, route and destination. Build a budget for both stages before ordering, even though the exact international figure is not known yet.

sections.heading: Stage one: product, domestic delivery and service choices
paragraphs: The original product price is set by the seller. Domestic delivery covers transport from that seller to the Superbuy warehouse. Some sellers offer free domestic shipping; others charge it separately. The current Superbuy fee guide says standard purchasing from mainstream platforms including Taobao, Tmall, JD and 1688 has no purchasing service fee. It lists different charges for second-hand platforms, unlisted sources and specialist purchasing services.

Optional product services sit beside those costs. The current list includes detailed photographs, re-inspection, detailed inspection, power-on checks, video and other special handling. These services are not automatically required. Use one when it answers a real question or reduces a specific risk. Adding every available service to a low-value item can cost more than the uncertainty it removes.

sections.heading: The warehouse changes what can be calculated
paragraphs: Before arrival, international shipping is only a rough scenario because the warehouse has not confirmed the received item’s weight and packaging. Once goods are stored, you can see warehouse data, review QC photos and decide which items belong in the same parcel. Superbuy currently advertises free QC photos and 90 days of free storage, giving users time to inspect and consolidate.

The fee guide says multiple items can be consolidated into one parcel without a consolidation fee. That may reduce repeated first-weight charges, but it does not make all combinations efficient. A parcel that mixes dense clothing with large empty retail boxes may be billed on volume. A very large parcel can also limit the available routes or become harder to handle. Consolidate deliberately, not automatically.

sections.heading: Actual weight versus volumetric weight
paragraphs: Carriers need to price both mass and space. Actual weight is what the parcel weighs on a scale. Volumetric weight converts the parcel’s length, width and height into a chargeable figure using the route’s divisor. A light but bulky box can therefore cost more than a smaller parcel with the same scale weight. Different routes can apply different units, rounding and volumetric rules, so one calculation should not be copied across every line.

Shoe boxes, rigid gift packaging, pillows and other low-density goods often increase volume. Vacuum packaging may reduce suitable soft goods, while folding or removing a retail box can reduce empty space. Those choices also reduce protection or change presentation. Shipping optimization is a trade-off between cost, item safety and whether original packaging matters to you.

sections.heading: How the shipping deposit and final charge work
paragraphs: Superbuy’s forwarding guide says the international shipping deposit is calculated from estimated weight, the selected method and the destination. Its current fee FAQ adds that the logistics provider’s official bill determines the final cost. After the parcel is packed and measured, the charges are reconciled: an overpayment can be refunded, while an underpayment can require the balance.

This means the deposit is not a bait-and-switch and it is not a guaranteed final quote. It is an operational estimate made before the carrier’s final data is available. Keep a small budget margin and check the account after packing. If the difference is large, compare the packed dimensions and services with what you requested before assuming the calculation is wrong.

sections.heading: Compare routes on more than price
paragraphs: The cheapest available line is not always the lowest-risk choice. Compare item restrictions, destination coverage, chargeable-weight method, tracking, typical delivery range, handoff carrier and compensation or insurance terms. A route for ordinary clothing may reject batteries, liquids, food or other sensitive goods. A duty-inclusive or tax-related label also needs to be read carefully; it does not remove the buyer’s responsibility to understand local import rules.

Use the current shipping calculator close to parcel submission because rates and available lines change. Do not copy a price from an old review or another country. Two buyers with similar product lists can receive different options because their parcel dimensions, destination, warehouse, declarations or restricted-item classifications differ.

sections.heading: Packaging decisions that can change cost and risk
paragraphs: Superbuy’s current value-added list includes free package removal and simple packaging, plus paid options such as bubble cushioning, EPE protection, corner protectors, stretch film, moisture barriers, vacuum packaging and wooden cases. The right choice depends on the contents. Flexible clothing may not need a heavy box. Ceramics, electronics and collectible packaging may need more structure, filler and moisture protection.

Do not optimize only for the smallest number. Removing every box can expose a structured product to crushing. Keeping every retail carton can increase volumetric weight. Write parcel remarks that state the priority: reduce volume for soft clothing, retain a specific collectible box, protect four corners, or keep items separated. Clear priorities help the warehouse make consistent packing choices.

sections.heading: Customs, VAT and declaration responsibilities
paragraphs: The international freight shown by an agent is not necessarily the complete import cost. Superbuy’s fee guide states that customs duties or VAT charged by the destination are borne by the recipient. Rules depend on country, item category, declared value and current law. No spreadsheet or old community post can guarantee that a parcel will pass without tax or inspection.

Use truthful product descriptions and follow the destination’s declaration rules. Avoid advice that promises a magic value or universal tax-free method. If a route includes a particular customs arrangement, read its current terms inside the platform before payment. The cost of compliance is part of the real delivered price.

sections.heading: A planning example without fake precision
paragraphs: Suppose you are considering several clothing items and one pair of shoes. First total the live product prices and domestic shipping. Add only the product services you actually need. Use the calculator to create a range for the likely combined weight, then compare a version with the shoe box and a version without it if box condition is not important. Leave room for packing materials and final measurement.

This is more useful than publishing a single invented shipping price. Rates depend on destination and date, and the final charge depends on real parcel data. Your planning output should be a range and a decision: which items to combine, which packaging to keep, which routes are eligible and how much margin to reserve.

sections.heading: The final cost-control checklist
paragraphs: Before ordering, check product price, domestic delivery, source-platform fee rules and item restrictions. At the warehouse, review weight, QC and storage deadlines. Before parcel submission, compare consolidation choices, package removal, protection needs, route rules, chargeable weight and destination taxes. After packing, review the final measured data and account reconciliation.

The most reliable way to reduce Superbuy shipping surprises is not to chase a secret coupon or copy another buyer’s parcel. It is to understand which cost is being quoted at each stage, keep the parcel compact without sacrificing necessary protection, and use current route data for your own destination.

sections.heading: Compare two Indonesia parcel scenarios
paragraphs: Make one scenario for the items packed together and another for a realistic split. Use the same destination and contents, then record the route, estimated packed weight, dimensions and selected protection. Add all parcel charges in the split scenario before comparing totals. Mark dimensions that remain uncertain and keep customs budgeting separate from the freight quote. A small difference between rough estimates is not a verified saving.

After packing, compare the updated measurements and final adjustment with your original inputs. Save the parcel reference and route with the payment record, then use the tracking guide for carrier handoff and delivery questions. Revisit the warehouse inventory as well: items excluded from this parcel still have their own storage deadlines. This prevents a shipping decision from leaving older goods without a next action.

superbuy-payment-fees-indonesia.title: Superbuy Payment and Fees for Indonesian Buyers
superbuy-payment-fees-indonesia.description: Plan Superbuy payments in IDR, compare the amount credited in CNY, separate purchase and shipping costs, and resolve pending charges without paying twice.

sections.heading: Start with the amount you need credited
paragraphs: For an Indonesian buyer, the useful payment question is how many rupiah leave the payment account for the amount credited to the shopping account. An attractive exchange rate means little if a separate processing charge changes the total. Before confirming a payment, record the debit currency, total debit, credited currency, credited amount and any fee shown. Compare methods using the same target amount and at approximately the same time. This gives you a practical comparison without assuming that one method is always cheapest.

Keep the product budget separate from the shipping reserve. Buying an item does not complete its journey to Indonesia. You may still need domestic delivery, optional inspection, international delivery and import charges. A sensible first order leaves money for these later stages instead of spending the whole budget on a large basket. This guide explains how to organize those decisions; it does not promise a fixed exchange rate or payment method for every account.

sections.heading: Separate purchase, warehouse and delivery costs
paragraphs: Superbuy's fee structure describes purchasing and international shipping as separate stages. At purchase, check the live item price, seller delivery charge and any purchasing service charge applicable to that source. At the warehouse, record optional services only when you choose them. At parcel submission, use the available route and packed parcel information to review the delivery estimate. Keep each amount beside the order or parcel it belongs to, so a later adjustment can be traced rather than mistaken for a duplicate charge.

For your own budget, add separate rows for currency conversion, payment processing and Indonesia import costs. These rows are planning categories, not a claim that every order incurs every charge. Some remain zero, while others remain unknown until you choose a route or receive an assessment. Mark unknown amounts clearly. A blank customs row is not evidence that customs will be free, just as a free purchasing service does not make international shipping free.

sections.heading: Check payment methods inside your account
paragraphs: The official Help Center currently lists payment guidance for top-ups, Wise, international credit cards and WeChat. That navigation does not establish that every option is available to every Indonesian customer. The methods and terms presented in your own payment flow are the relevant evidence. Read the currency, limits, fees and recipient instructions before continuing. Do not assume that a method mentioned in an old video, spreadsheet or comment is still supported for your account or transaction.

If the payment flow asks you to transfer money, match the recipient details against the instructions displayed after signing in yourself. A screenshot forwarded by another person is not a substitute. Use a payment account you are entitled to use and preserve the transaction reference. Do not send full card details, passwords or authentication codes in a support message. When you only need help matching a payment, a reference, date, amount and currency are more useful than unnecessary financial information.

sections.heading: Compare total IDR debit with CNY credit
paragraphs: Create a small comparison with one row per available payment method. Write the intended CNY credit, the displayed IDR debit if provided, any separately disclosed fee and the time you checked. Divide the total rupiah debit by the CNY credit to obtain an effective rupiah cost per credited yuan. Compare like with like: a small top-up and a much larger top-up may have different effective costs where a fixed charge applies. Never treat a promotional exchange quote as your actual completed transaction.

An illustrative comparison can use two unnamed methods, A and B, without inventing a current provider rate. If both credit the same CNY amount, the smaller final IDR debit is cheaper for that particular quote. If the debit currencies differ, first work out what your bank will actually charge and whether that remains uncertain. Record the settled debit later. This method helps you notice differences without presenting an example number as today's Indonesian payment rate.

sections.heading: Read optional charges before selecting them
paragraphs: Optional warehouse services should answer a specific need. An additional photo may help when a size label is unreadable; stronger packaging may be appropriate for a fragile item. Write down the question each service will answer, then check its price at the point of selection. Avoid selecting several services because their names sound reassuring. A photograph cannot settle every concern about material quality, and adding packaging cannot guarantee that a parcel will arrive undamaged.

Distinguish the absence of a standard purchasing fee from the absence of all service fees. Superbuy's fee page describes different treatment for standard purchasing and some other purchasing arrangements. Use the charge attached to your actual order instead of applying a blanket rule from a guide. If the description and amount do not match your understanding, clarify before paying. Save the displayed breakdown so you can compare it with the later order record rather than relying on memory.

sections.heading: Resolve a pending payment before trying again
paragraphs: When a payment appears pending, start by identifying which system shows that status. Your bank may show an authorization, the payment provider may show a transfer in progress, and the shopping account may show no credit yet. These observations are different. Record the exact status and time in each place. Do not label a payment successful merely because money appears reserved, and do not label it failed solely because a page did not refresh immediately.

Before repeating the transaction, check the payment history and contact the relevant provider through its verified channel if the state remains unclear. Include the reference, amount, currency and timestamp, plus a screenshot with unrelated information hidden. Ask a precise question: whether this transaction was received and whether another payment is required. Repeated attempts can make reconciliation harder. There is no universal waiting period in this guide because processing depends on the chosen method and the actual transaction.

sections.heading: Treat the shipping deposit as a separate record
paragraphs: Superbuy's fee explanation says the initial shipping payment can be reconciled against the logistics provider's final bill. Your budget should therefore distinguish an estimate, a deposit and a final charge. Save the selected line, destination, contents and weight information with the parcel number. When an adjustment appears, compare it against that same parcel. A shipping refund is different from a refund for a returned product, even if both eventually affect the same account balance.

For an Indonesia parcel, compare available routes using the actual contents and destination. Do not budget from another shopper's screenshot without matching dimensions, weight, date and service conditions. Leave a reserve for unresolved costs rather than assuming the first estimate is exact. If a quoted route is unavailable after the contents change, redo the comparison before submitting. Adding one bulky item can change the parcel decision even when its purchase price is small.

sections.heading: Reconcile refunds without assuming a destination
paragraphs: Keep a refund record with the original order, reason, requested amount, approved amount and current status. Then check where the refund is credited under the applicable terms. A refund to an account balance and a reversal to the original payment method are different outcomes. Do not assume that seeing an approved refund means the money has reached your Indonesian bank. Read the transaction history and the method-specific instructions before drawing that conclusion.

When several transactions overlap, maintain one reference per movement. Label purchases, top-ups, shipping deposits, adjustments and refunds separately. This makes it possible to answer a practical question such as whether a returned shoe order reduced the amount needed for a later parcel. If the records do not reconcile, send support the smallest relevant set of transactions and state the discrepancy. A clear ledger usually explains the problem better than a long account history with no highlighted issue.

sections.heading: Finish with a payment checklist
paragraphs: Before paying, confirm the exact product option, the amount due now and the amounts still needed later. Review the payment method inside your own account, compare the total debit with the credit received, and save the transaction reference. After paying, match the credit or order payment to that reference. Before international shipping, repeat the cost review using the parcel details. After delivery, reconcile adjustments and refunds so your final cost reflects settled amounts rather than early estimates.

Use the separate shipping-cost and Indonesia customs guides for the next budgeting steps. This payment guide supports the narrower decision of how to understand and document charges. Product discovery on superbuys.id leads to cnfanshp.com; that catalog is separate from your Superbuy account. Opening a catalog listing does not make a payment or create a warehouse order. Keeping those destinations distinct prevents a product browsing page from being mistaken for an official payment screen.

superbuy-shoe-size-qc-guide.title: Superbuy Shoe Spreadsheet: Sizing and QC Checks
superbuy-shoe-size-qc-guide.description: Choose shoe sizes from seller measurements, check both shoes in warehouse QC photos, and decide whether to keep the box before shipping to Indonesia.

sections.heading: Begin with fit requirements, then browse shoes
paragraphs: A Superbuy shoe spreadsheet is useful for finding candidates, but it cannot choose your size. Start with what you need the shoes to do: everyday walking, occasional wear or a particular outfit. Note the fit problems you already encounter, such as a narrow forefoot or a loose heel. Then browse a small group of listings. A shortlist based on usable measurements is easier to evaluate than a long collection of attractive images with no information about fit.

This guide follows one pair from discovery to the warehouse decision. The goal is to identify the exact size and visible condition before international shipping to Indonesia. It does not authenticate a brand, certify sporting performance or promise comfort from photographs. A familiar logo and a popular spreadsheet row are not substitutes for measurements, a clear listing and a return decision made while the item remains accessible to the seller.

sections.heading: Measure both feet consistently
paragraphs: Use the seller's measuring instructions when available. For a basic comparison, measure both feet while standing on a level surface with the socks you expect to wear. Keep the heel position consistent and record length in millimetres or centimetres, stating the unit. Repeat the measurement to catch a misplaced mark. Note any difference between the two feet instead of averaging it away. Also record width concerns, because matching length alone does not establish that the shape will suit you.

Do not automatically add a fixed amount to every measurement. A chart may already include a fit allowance, or it may describe the foot length associated with each option. Adding another allowance without understanding the chart can produce the wrong choice. Compare the seller's explanation with the chart labels. If the relationship is unclear, ask whether the listed number refers to recommended foot length, insole length or another measurement before selecting the size.

sections.heading: Read the size chart for the exact listing
paragraphs: Treat EU, UK and US labels as size systems that need interpretation, not interchangeable numbers. A seller may use a conversion table that differs from another listing. Read the chart for the actual model and option you intend to buy, including any distinction between adult and children's sizing. Save the chart with the product URL and date. A generic conversion graphic found elsewhere can help you understand the systems, but it cannot override a seller-specific specification.

Check whether the page includes several models or batches under one title. A chart for the first photograph may not apply to every selectable option. Make a short record containing the option name, size label, relevant measurement and colour. If the product page has no usable measurements, treat that as an unresolved purchase risk. Buying the same nominal size as a previous pair from a different seller is a guess, even when both labels look familiar.

sections.heading: Separate foot, insole and outsole measurements
paragraphs: Foot length, insole length and outsole length describe different things. The external sole includes construction that is not usable interior space. An insole may curve at the heel or sit differently inside the shoe. A photograph of an outsole beside a ruler therefore cannot directly establish the foot length the shoe accommodates. Keep every measurement labelled so that a later warehouse photo is compared with the right reference rather than with an unrelated number.

If one measurement determines whether you keep the pair, request that specific measurement and explain the method. For example, ask for a removable insole to be laid flat beside a ruler only if removal is possible without damage and the service permits it. Do not ask staff to force apart a glued component. Even a well-taken ruler photograph has limits from angle and placement. Use it to resolve a meaningful mismatch, not to claim millimetre-perfect fit certainty.

sections.heading: Record the option before placing the order
paragraphs: Save the live listing, selected size, colour, quantity and model identifier in one place. Include the size chart and any seller clarification that affected your choice. Write a concise order remark when a translated option name is ambiguous. It is more useful to identify the exact option code than to say that you want the pair shown in a screenshot containing several shoes. Confirm that the price belongs to a complete pair and the chosen variant.

Before paying, review the seller's applicable return conditions and any service warning shown for the order. Do not assume a custom or unusual purchase can be returned simply because an ordinary listing allows it. Keep the first order manageable while you learn the process. Several pairs ordered from incomplete charts create several independent sizing risks; placing them together does not make those uncertainties disappear or guarantee that one parcel will be economical.

sections.heading: Inspect both shoes when QC photographs arrive
paragraphs: Begin warehouse QC with identity and quantity. Confirm that the images show a pair, that both shoes have the expected design, and that readable labels match the selected size. Look for mismatched left and right labels or visibly different shapes. Then compare the colour and distinctive construction with the saved listing. Use several angles where available. A small label in an overview image may require a closer photo before it provides reliable evidence.

Move on to visible condition: toe shape, heel alignment, outsole attachment, fastening hardware, obvious tears, stains and damage. Consider whether a mark could be glare or packing debris before drawing a conclusion. A visible concern deserves a specific question, such as a close view of one area from another angle. Standard photos cannot establish hidden materials, long-term sole strength or how the shoe feels on your foot. Keep the conclusion within what the images actually show.

sections.heading: Ask for one useful additional view
paragraphs: An additional photo is most helpful when you can name the fact it should reveal. Request readable labels on both shoes, a particular seam, the outsole pattern or a ruler view tied to the seller's chart. Give the order number and identify the side or component. A broad request to check whether the shoes are good leaves the warehouse guessing about your standard. Decide in advance what result would lead you to keep, question or return the pair.

Superbuy's fee page lists optional detailed photographs, with the live service selection controlling the applicable charge. Review that price before ordering the image. More photos do not solve every uncertainty. If your concern is authenticity or performance under running loads, repeated exterior images cannot establish the answer. The appropriate decision may be to avoid that purchase or choose a seller whose product information and terms support your requirements more clearly.

sections.heading: Make the box decision before parcel submission
paragraphs: The shoes and their retail box are separate packing decisions. Keeping a box may matter for storage, gifting or protecting a particular structure, but it can add volume. Removing it may reduce bulk while requiring another form of protection. Decide what you need to preserve before asking for any irreversible packaging change. If a return is still being considered, resolve that first and check the applicable packaging requirements rather than discarding useful evidence prematurely.

Compare the packed parcel configurations using actual route conditions. Two shoe boxes may affect chargeable weight differently from one pair packed with flexible clothing. Do not assume box removal produces a fixed saving or that combining everything always costs less. Indonesia destination restrictions and import treatment remain separate checks. A shipping line accepting the parcel is not a guarantee of customs clearance, and a low declared value is not a legitimate way to solve a high budget.

sections.heading: Approve with a clear decision record
paragraphs: Make your final warehouse decision from a short record: selected option, saved chart, visible size labels, relevant measurement, condition concerns and packaging choice. Approve only after the decisive visible checks are resolved. If there is a mismatch, report the observable issue with the order number and supporting image before international shipping. Ask about the available remedy and timing. A seller may need to respond, so do not postpone that decision until your planned dispatch day.

Browse the shoe category when you are ready to compare listings, and use the general QC checklist for other product types. The catalog link opens cnfanshp.com for discovery; ordering, payment and warehouse decisions belong in the appropriate service account. Keeping this distinction clear helps you move from a shoe spreadsheet to a documented purchase. The strongest outcome is a pair chosen from understood measurements, checked against its actual order and packed according to its needs.

superbuy-warehouse-consolidation-guide.title: Superbuy Warehouse and Parcel Consolidation for Indonesia
superbuy-warehouse-consolidation-guide.description: Track storage deadlines, resolve QC issues, compare combined and separate parcels, and prepare clear packing instructions before shipping to Indonesia.

sections.heading: Build a warehouse inventory before combining items
paragraphs: Parcel consolidation means deciding which received items should travel together. Start with the warehouse inventory rather than the number of products you originally ordered. Record the order reference, received quantity, inspection status, storage date and any unresolved issue for each item. A seller shipment still travelling to the warehouse is not ready to pack. An item with an unanswered size question is physically present but may still be unsuitable for the parcel you intend to approve.

For Indonesian buyers, add a destination column for any parcel that may be sent to a different recipient or address. Do not mix items simply because they arrived during the same week. A useful inventory makes three groups visible: ready to ship, waiting for information, and waiting for a seller or support decision. Those groups can change as evidence arrives. Review them before paying for packaging so that an unresolved return does not become part of an international shipment.

sections.heading: Keep each item's storage deadline visible
paragraphs: The official Superbuy fee guide currently describes 90 days of free storage and a normal maximum storage period of 180 days. Extension arrangements and storage charges are separate matters. The date and terms shown for your actual item should guide action. Do not assume that adding a new purchase restarts the clock for older goods or that buying an extension necessarily makes the extended period free. Check what the selected service changes before paying for it.

Maintain a deadline beside every stored order, including older items you temporarily excluded from a parcel. Choose your own earlier review date to leave time for questions, seller responses and packing decisions. A calendar reminder is more reliable than remembering the age of a mixed basket. If you cannot ship in time, ask about the available options while there is still time to act. Do not interpret an estimated shopping schedule as permission to leave goods indefinitely.

sections.heading: Resolve QC and returns before packing
paragraphs: Review each item against its saved order record before including it. Check the variant, quantity, visible condition and any decisive measurement. If you are considering a return, keep the item out of the parcel until the remedy and applicable terms are clear. Packaging changes can remove useful evidence or affect return eligibility. Avoid removing labels or retail packaging while still deciding whether the seller sent the correct item.

Use precise notes when an item is on hold. Write the order reference, the missing fact and the action requested, such as a readable size label or a response about a visibly wrong colour. This keeps the hold separate from a general feeling of uncertainty. When support resolves the issue, update the inventory and save the decision. Do not assume that warehouse presence, completed photos and approval to ship are interchangeable statuses; each answers a different operational question.

sections.heading: Compare one combined parcel with a realistic split
paragraphs: Create two practical packing scenarios using the same set of items. In the first, combine compatible goods. In the second, separate a bulky, fragile or restricted item if its requirements differ. Record the estimated packed weight, outer dimensions, available routes and selected protection for each scenario. Compare the total across all parcels in the split option. Comparing one combined quote with only the cheaper half of a split shipment gives a misleading result.

Consolidation can avoid repeated starting charges, but the official description does not guarantee a saving for every combination. Larger dimensions, different route eligibility or extra protection can change the outcome. The most useful comparison includes the items you actually have, not an imagined average parcel. If dimensions remain unknown, mark the result provisional. A small difference between rough estimates may not justify a more complicated packing arrangement or increased risk to a fragile item.

sections.heading: Understand why volume changes the decision
paragraphs: Actual weight measures mass; volumetric weight represents the space occupied under a route's charging rules. A light but large parcel can therefore have a different chargeable weight from its scale reading. Superbuy's calculator asks for dimensions as well as weight, destination and item category. Use the divisor and rounding rules attached to the selected route rather than assuming that one formula applies to every service. Keep centimetres and grams consistent with the fields you enter.

Think about the outer package rather than adding product dimensions mechanically. Flexible garments may fit around a rigid box, while two boxes may leave unused space or require a larger carton. Protective material also takes space. Ask for information that will reduce the uncertainty that matters to your decision, such as whether a retail box must be retained. Avoid presenting a hypothetical volume calculation as a warehouse measurement or promising an exact saving before the final package exists.

sections.heading: Choose protection item by item
paragraphs: Write packing instructions around the physical needs of the contents. A flexible garment, a structured shoe and a fragile accessory do not require identical treatment. Identify which retail packaging can be removed, which must remain intact and which surfaces need protection from pressure or contact. Clear instructions reduce the chance that a general request for the smallest box conflicts with the need to preserve a delicate component. Check the available services and charges before selecting them.

Keep instructions short enough to verify. For example, separate orders that may have unnecessary outer packaging removed from orders whose retail boxes must remain intact. Do not combine contradictory requests such as preserving every box unchanged while also asking for maximum compression. Where the service cannot meet both goals, choose the priority or ask for clarification. No packaging option eliminates transport risk, and adding every available service can increase cost without addressing the item's actual vulnerability.

sections.heading: Check Indonesia route eligibility for the whole parcel
paragraphs: Review the available routes using the complete contents and the Indonesian destination. One item can change the options for everything packed with it. Batteries, liquids and other restricted categories may require different handling, but the exact restriction must come from the current route information and import rules. Do not infer acceptance from a broad category name or another customer's shipment. If one item's eligibility is unclear, resolve it before combining the parcel.

Check the recipient name, phone number, postcode and address detail carefully. Use consistent item descriptions and values supported by purchase records. Combining goods does not erase their individual identities or import obligations. Keep invoices and the packing list together so that a request about one item can be answered without reconstructing the entire shopping history. If a route or recipient field changes, review the parcel again rather than assuming the earlier comparison remains valid.

sections.heading: Save the final parcel configuration
paragraphs: Before submission, save the item list and the selected packaging instructions. Record the parcel reference when it becomes available, along with the route, destination and initial shipping payment. After packing, compare any updated weight, dimensions or charge with the earlier estimate. A change is easier to understand when the original inputs are visible. Ask a focused question if the final parcel includes an unexpected item or a service you did not intend to select.

Separate the shipping deposit from the final settled cost in your records. Superbuy describes reconciliation after the logistics provider's bill, so a first payment should not automatically be treated as the final amount. Also preserve the inventory of goods left behind. Submitting one parcel does not solve the storage deadline for excluded items. Update their next action immediately, whether that is a return request, another photograph, a separate shipment or a storage inquiry.

sections.heading: Use a repeatable release checklist
paragraphs: Release a parcel only after checking contents, QC decisions, storage deadlines, packing instructions, route eligibility, address and remaining budget. Keep the list short enough to use every time. A useful final question is whether any unresolved decision has simply been hidden inside the combined parcel. If the answer is yes, pause that item and resolve it. The purpose of consolidation is a deliberate parcel configuration, not merely clearing the warehouse screen as quickly as possible.

For the next step, use the shipping-cost guide to compare charges and the tracking guide to follow the handoff after dispatch. Product browsing on cnfanshp.com remains separate from warehouse operations in your service account. This distinction matters when moving between the guide and a catalog. A successful consolidation decision leaves you with a clear list of what shipped, what stayed behind, why the packaging was chosen and which evidence supports the final approval.

superbuy-tracking-indonesia.title: How to Track a Superbuy Parcel to Indonesia
superbuy-tracking-indonesia.description: Match order and parcel numbers, interpret tracking evidence, investigate missing updates, and prepare a clear support request for an Indonesia delivery.

sections.heading: Start with the correct number and shipping stage
paragraphs: To track a Superbuy parcel to Indonesia, first identify which journey you are checking. Seller delivery to the warehouse is different from international delivery to your address. The shopping order reference, domestic tracking number, warehouse parcel reference and international tracking number can identify different records. Put them in separate fields instead of copying whichever number is easiest to find. A domestic delivery marked complete may only mean the goods reached the warehouse, not that the Indonesian shipment arrived.

The official Superbuy parcel tracking page accepts a tracking number or parcel number. Begin with the reference shown in your own parcel details and preserve the route name beside it. This guide explains how to organize and interpret the available evidence. It does not provide a private account lookup or promise a delivery date. Tracking events, wording and handoffs depend on the actual carrier and route, so the instructions attached to that shipment remain important.

sections.heading: Separate parcel preparation from carrier movement
paragraphs: A submitted parcel request and a carrier scan are different forms of evidence. The first can show that you asked for shipment; the second can show an event recorded by a logistics operator. Read the exact wording and location instead of treating every update as proof that the parcel has left China. A number assigned to a parcel does not by itself establish physical acceptance, departure or arrival in Indonesia. Look for the event that supports the conclusion you need.

Keep a short timeline with the timestamp, source and wording of each meaningful update. If the account and carrier page show different information, save both rather than overwriting one with the other. They may describe different stages or update at different times. Ask which stage is confirmed when the evidence remains ambiguous. Avoid translating a broad phrase into a precise transport event that the source does not actually state.

sections.heading: Use the route's actual carrier information
paragraphs: Open the carrier or delivery partner identified in your parcel details, using its verified website or application. Do not choose a carrier solely because a tracking number resembles one you used before. Where a local tracking number is supplied after a handoff, save it alongside the original reference. That relationship helps you connect international progress with final delivery. It also gives support a clearer record if one system recognizes the parcel and another does not.

Do not assume that every shipment to Indonesia uses the same final delivery company. Follow the partner named for your specific route. A third-party tracking page may be convenient, but compare a concerning event with the carrier's own information where possible. Be careful about unsolicited payment links in tracking messages. Navigate to the verified service yourself and match the parcel details before taking action, especially if the message requests money or personal information.

sections.heading: Diagnose a tracking number with no result
paragraphs: When a lookup returns no result, check the reference character by character. Remove accidental spaces, distinguish letters from similar digits and confirm that you selected the correct record. Then check whether the number is intended for Superbuy's parcel lookup, a domestic seller shipment or the international carrier. A valid account reference may not be a carrier tracking number. This simple distinction can explain a failed search without requiring any conclusion about the physical parcel.

If the number and lookup are correct, compare the account status with the route's current instructions. The available data may not yet show a carrier event, but that alone does not tell you why. Save the failed lookup and the parcel status with a timestamp. If you need assistance, ask whether the number is active, whether a different carrier reference is available and what handoff has been confirmed. Do not create a new parcel request merely to obtain another number.

sections.heading: Investigate a tracking feed that stopped updating
paragraphs: For a feed with earlier events, identify the last meaningful scan rather than counting days from the original product purchase. Record its date, location and exact text. Compare the elapsed time with the information published for your selected route and any current service notice. There is no universal number of silent days that proves a parcel is lost. A long gap is a reason to investigate with the relevant evidence, not permission to invent the parcel's location.

Check whether a handoff introduced another tracking number or delivery partner. If both systems remain unchanged, ask support what event is last confirmed and whether an investigation is appropriate under the route's terms. Keep the question specific to your parcel. Another shopper's faster delivery may be interesting but does not establish the expected timing for different contents, dates, routes or addresses. Save your own timeline so repeated support conversations do not start from scratch.

sections.heading: Handle customs information requests carefully
paragraphs: An event mentioning customs or documentation should be read with the actual notice, not with assumptions from a forum. Identify who is asking, which parcel the request concerns, what document is missing and which verified channel accepts the response. Keep the invoice, payment evidence, item description and shipping details available. Provide accurate information that matches the purchase and contents. Do not alter values or rename goods to make a request appear easier to resolve.

Indonesian import charges and restrictions depend on the applicable rules and the actual goods. A tracking label alone does not tell you the final amount due or guarantee release. Use the customs guide for the document checklist, then verify the specific assessment through the responsible authority or operator. If the notice seems inconsistent, ask for clarification through a verified channel. Avoid sending identity documents or payment information to an unverified sender just because the message includes a familiar tracking number.

sections.heading: Respond to delivery exceptions with useful details
paragraphs: When a carrier reports an address or delivery problem, compare the submitted address with the destination shown in the shipment record. Check the postcode, building detail, recipient phone number and any permitted delivery instructions. Contact the actual delivery partner using the reference it recognizes. Explain the specific mismatch or access issue and ask what correction is available. Do not assume that editing your shopping account profile changes an already dispatched parcel's label.

If a parcel is marked delivered but you have not received it, check the event details and any proof made available by the carrier. Ask household members or the authorized reception point where appropriate, then report the discrepancy promptly through the applicable process. Save the timestamp and reference. Do not assert theft or loss from the status alone; describe what is known, such as a delivery record with no parcel at the stated receiving location.

sections.heading: Preserve packaging and evidence after arrival
paragraphs: At delivery, inspect the outer package and document visible damage before discarding anything. Photograph the label, affected area and contents where relevant, keeping private address information out of public posts. Match received items against the parcel list. If something is missing or damaged, preserve the packaging and the relevant warehouse photos until the applicable claim or support process is complete. A clear sequence of evidence is more useful than a single close-up with no parcel identity.

Check the terms and reporting deadlines associated with the actual route or protection service. This guide does not assume that every problem qualifies for compensation or that every service uses the same deadline. Submit a factual account of the issue and the requested help. Keep copies of the response and case reference. Avoid replacing an investigation with repeated public claims that go beyond the evidence; the useful objective is to establish what happened and which remedy applies.

sections.heading: Send a concise tracking support request
paragraphs: Prepare one message containing the parcel reference, route, international and local tracking numbers if available, last confirmed event, date checked and the specific problem. Attach only the relevant screenshots with unnecessary personal information hidden. State what you want clarified: carrier acceptance, a missing local number, an unchanged scan, a document request or a delivery discrepancy. These are different questions and should not be bundled into a vague statement that tracking is broken.

After support replies, add the response and next action to your timeline. Set your next check according to that instruction and the route's conditions rather than repeatedly refreshing several sites without a plan. Keep payment, customs and delivery records until the matter is resolved. The practical result of good tracking is an organized account of confirmed events and open questions, with enough detail for the responsible party to investigate your Indonesia parcel efficiently.

cara-belanja-di-superbuy.title: How to Buy with Superbuy from Indonesia
cara-belanja-di-superbuy.description: Follow a first Superbuy order from Taobao or 1688 through payment, warehouse QC, parcel preparation and shipping to Indonesia.

sections.heading: Understand the shopping agent service
paragraphs: Ordering through Superbuy differs from checking out directly at an Indonesian store. With the shopping agent service, you submit a Chinese marketplace listing and select a variant; the agent purchases it from the third-party seller. The goods first travel to a warehouse in China. You can then review inspection information and QC photos, store several orders, prepare a parcel and select international shipping to Indonesia. Parcel forwarding is a separate service for goods you have already purchased yourself.

This two-stage flow means there are two payments that need to be distinguished. The first payment usually includes the price of the goods, domestic shipping from the seller to the warehouse, and optional product services. The second payment is made when the goods have been selected as an international package. The value is influenced by destination, weight, volume, type of goods, packaging, and available routes. Understanding the separation from the outset helps prevent the assumption that prices on Taobao or 1688 include home delivery.

sections.heading: Find current Taobao or 1688 listings
paragraphs: To buy Taobao via Superbuy, start from the active product link, not a screenshot or old title. Paste the listing URL into the Superbuy product search or order field and wait for the system to read the product information. If the page is not read automatically, data may need to be entered manually. Make sure the item name, price, color, size, quantity, domestic shipping, as well as seller's note match the source listing before paying for the order.

Buying from 1688 through Superbuy follows a similar basic process, but wholesale listings often have minimum quantities, price tiers, or mixed options. Check whether the price applies to one unit or package, whether the minimum quantity is calculated per color, and whether the seller asks for additional specifications. Spreadsheets or product indexes can speed up searches, but current listings remain the reference for product details. If the selection on the index is different from the marketplace, use the latest information on the seller's page.

sections.heading: Choose the exact variant and measurements
paragraphs: The most expensive mistakes often happen before the goods are bought: the color, size, model, or quantity chosen does not match the buyer’s intentions. Save the selected screenshot and write a brief note with a clear order, e.g. black color, size 42, one pair, no boxes if available. Do not use descriptions like 'same as photo' if the listing has many photos and options.

Size labels used by Chinese sellers may differ from those you normally use in Indonesia. Compare the seller's size chart and physical measurements, not just label S, M, L or shoe number. For clothing, note the width of the chest, length, shoulders, and other determining parts. For shoes, use the length of the foot and if necessary ask for insole measurements after the goods arrive. Automatic translations are useful as a help, but figures, variation pictures, and written confirmations are easier to verify.

sections.heading: Budget the purchase stage realistically
paragraphs: The Superbuy cost guide reviewed in October 2026 states that standard purchases from major sources such as Taobao, Tmall, JD, and 1688 are not charged the standard purchase fee. But that does not mean the whole process is cost-free. The price of goods, domestic shipping, changes in exchange rates or payment methods, detailed photos, special inspections, and additional services can still affect the amount paid.

Record costs in both the source currency and your payment currency. Separate the price of goods from other costs so that changes are easily tracked. Do not just compare the numbers on the product card, because certain variants may have different prices. If the seller changes the price or shipping after the order is placed, read the agent's message and decide based on the new total. Cancel or ask for clarification before purchasing if important details are not correct.

sections.heading: Follow the order to the warehouse
paragraphs: After payment, the agent places the order with the seller. Time to warehouse is affected by stock, vendor processing time, and domestic delivery in China. Order status should be read as a milestone, not a date guarantee. If the seller has not shipped or the variant is out of stock, the agent can request a new decision. Reply to important messages quickly so that the waiting time does not increase without direction.

When the goods are received in the warehouse, check that the quantity and basic identity match. The reviewed Superbuy service information describes free QC photos after the warehouse inspection. These photos show the item that actually arrived, but do not prove authenticity, material composition, internal function, or durability. Keep pictures of listings and order records so that warehouse photos have a clear comparison.

sections.heading: Use QC photos to make a decision
paragraphs: Start the QC check with identity: model, color, size, quantity, and accessories. Then look at the general shape, symmetry, stains, damage, visible stitching, and condition of the packaging if it is important. If one defining detail is not visible, ask for additional specific photos, such as a size label from up close or a ruler along the insole. A request for a “quality check” is too general to produce comparable evidence.

The inspection should result in one of three decisions: accept the goods, request additional evidence, or ask after-sales support to review the issue. Return policies follow the marketplace of origin and the seller, so do not delay when discrepancies are apparent. Second-hand goods or special categories may have stricter regulations. Document order numbers, photos, and apparent differences rather than making claims that cannot be proven by camera.

sections.heading: Manage storage and consolidation deadlines
paragraphs: The cost guide reviewed in October 2026 states 90 days of free storage. This period allows time to wait for several orders, check QC, and combine qualified products into one package. Consolidation can reduce the repeated starting charges, but it does not always make freight cheaper. Large packages or combinations of sensitive goods can limit the route and increase volumetric weight.

Don't wait until the end of the free period without a plan. Record the date of arrival of each item and group it by type and available shipping route. Batteries, liquids, cosmetics, food, or restricted categories may require different handling. Compare a combined package with two separate packages based on the route that actually appears for Indonesia, not on the past experience of other buyers.

sections.heading: Prepare the parcel and compare Indonesia routes
paragraphs: Before shipping, determine the items to be included, box requirements, corner protection, cushioning, vacuum, retail packaging removal, and moisture protection. Choose according to the physical needs of the contents. Soft clothing may be safely compacted, while shoes, electronics, fragile items, or collection boxes may require additional structure. The smallest package isn't necessarily the safest package.

Compare routes through accepted goods categories, weight and size limits, how to calculate volumetric weight, tracking, time estimates, compensation, as well as availability to destination zip codes. Initial shipping is an estimate based on package data; after packing, actual weight and dimensions may cause reconciliation. Keep a reserve fund and do not assume that one model tariff applies to all of Indonesia or throughout the year.

sections.heading: Keep customs and delivery records
paragraphs: Parcels entering Indonesia are imported goods. Use accurate descriptions and values, retain transaction evidence, and include possible import duty, value-added tax and other applicable charges in the total delivery budget. Treatment depends on customs value and classification and can change. Check current Bea Cukai information before shipping, particularly for cosmetics, textiles, footwear, bags, electronics or goods requiring specific permits.

After the package is sent, keep tracking number, content details, QC photo, weight, dimensions, route, declaration, and proof of payment. Monitor status changes without treating a gap between scans as proof of loss. If there is a problem, contact the relevant service with the package number and structured proof. With these records, ordering from Indonesia becomes a traceable process: find, verify, buy, check QC, package, calculate costs, declare correctly, and track.

sections.heading: Separate product discovery from account actions
paragraphs: The product and search links on superbuys.id open the cnfanshp.com catalog. The catalog is different from the Superbuy account for paying orders, checking inventory, and sending packages. Opening a listing does not automatically create an order. Save the source link and the correct variant, size and quantity before continuing in the appropriate service account.

Make simple notes with columns for product links, options, purchase costs, inventory status, and next action. If any of the data is unclear, resolve that question before paying or approving the shipment. Use the payment guide to check the costs and tracking guide after the parcel is handed to the shipping provider.

pajak-bea-cukai-superbuy-indonesia.title: Superbuy Indonesia Customs: Duties, VAT and Documents
pajak-bea-cukai-superbuy-indonesia.description: Understand Indonesia parcel duties, the VAT tax base, supporting documents and landed-cost budgeting before shipping a Superbuy parcel.

sections.heading: Treat an Indonesia parcel as imported goods
paragraphs: A parcel sent from a Superbuy warehouse to an Indonesian address enters Indonesia as imported goods. Payments already made to the seller, agent or logistics provider do not automatically remove destination obligations. Budget for import duty, value-added tax (PPN), income tax (PPh) where applicable, operator handling charges and any documents required for the actual goods.

This guide compares the official Bea Cukai Barang Kiriman overview and detailed FAQ, checked on 6 October 2026. The overview’s VAT rate should be read alongside the tax-base explanation in the FAQ. Use the rules, classification and official assessment that apply to your parcel; general figures are not a promise of the final bill.

sections.heading: Separate product price, freight and customs value
paragraphs: Prices seen on Taobao or 1688 are only one component. Other components include domestic delivery to the warehouse, optional services, international shipping and import charges. To estimate the landed cost, note each component separately and keep proof of transaction. Customs value and the tax bases follow the applicable rules; do not assume that the price of a product is always the only figure that counts.

Use the correct currency, exchange rate, description, quantity and category. Proof of order, invoices, payment records, package contents, and shipping details help when the operator or agent asks for clarification. Avoid declarations that intentionally undervalue or disguise the goods. In addition to risking reassessment and delays, inaccurate descriptions can complicate claims if parcels are damaged or lost.

sections.heading: Understand value thresholds and general import duty
